plates.reference: Own code graphic: on period paper, an inked molecular diagram shows red blood cell surface antigens (~2 million A or B sugar markers per cell: Type A with A pegs, Type B with B spheres, Type AB with both, Type O smooth) and Y-shaped plasma antibodies (anti-B, anti-A, none, both), demonstrating why Type O red cells pass unattacked as universal donor.

teach_overlay.label: TYPE A, B, AB, O (~2M ANTIGEN SITES/CELL) & ANTI-A / ANTI-B ANTIBODIES
teach_overlay.detail: Inked molecular diagram on period paper showing red blood cell surface antigens (A pegs, B spheres, AB both, O smooth) and Y-shaped plasma antibodies demonstrating why Type O red cells are universal donor
teach_overlay.scale: each red blood cell carries around 2 million microscopic A or B sugar markers on its skin — if the wrong antibody locks on, millions of cells glue together like Velcro
